baseline_note: The skill is new; arm 'base' is stub-perf.md, a 2-line prompt with no skill body. It measures the value the full skill adds over the bare model. From v2 onward the baseline is the last committed skill version.

arms.base: stub-perf.md - minimal prompt, no skill body
arms.v2: v1 + cold-file pattern sweep + record dismissals in Not Found (4bc5785)

skill_changes_summary: New skill: Abseil Performance Hints distilled into hot/cold discipline, latency-table estimates, 6-category taxonomy, and a P1-P4 impact-vs-effort priority matrix. New scorer priority_score.py measures the ordering promise directly.
known_limitations: One sample per arm: run-to-run deltas under ~10% are noise; borderline commit decisions get a duplicate -b run.
perfburn carries no in-source BUG annotations, so recall is a real signal there; eventbus still carries them, so its recall saturates and is a sanity check only.
strict_precision treats the perfburn ground truth as exhaustive; a real unplanted find must be recorded in the corrections array, not counted against precision.

10 ground-truth labels were corrected in this iteration after arithmetic review (see corrections array); the original labels were gut-calibrated and the v1 report's estimates exposed them. Residual circularity risk is bounded by requiring an arithmetic justification independent of the model's claim for every correction.
After the corrections no planted issue derives to P4; planting a true P4 (and a client-server DB variant where N+1 really costs a network round trip) is future test-surface work.

gt_score keyword matching is loose by design; iteration-6 tightened it with a perfburn-specific line_window of 6 and a domain-generic STOP-word extension, but matches are still reviewed via benchmark.json's matched/unmatched lists.
